newsitem.title: USA: Tosco starts layoffs at California refineries.
newsitem.headline: Tosco starts layoffs at California refineries.

text.p: Tosco Corp began laying off 130 California refinery workers Tuesday, after forcing union officials last night to accept a final contract amid threats the company would shut the Rodeo, Calif. plant, union officials said.
"Tosco officials threatened to shutdown the Rodeo refinery if the union didn't agree to their terms last night," said Kelly Quinn, a union official in Los Angeles.
He said Tosco plans to lay off up to 130 refinery workers at the four California plants it will acquire from Unocal March 31. The layoffs will be staggered over the next couple days.

The union late Monday accepted a tentative contract from Tosco because "they felt the threat Tosco made was serious and they didn't know what else to do," Quinn said, adding Tosco declined to meet further.

Except for changes in medical benefits, last night's contract remains unchanged from earlier Tosco offers, which the union rejected, claiming they contained sub-standard benefits and too many job cuts.
Tosco began laying off maintenance workers early Monday but Quinn said 75 percent of layoffs are among staff who operate the plant's processing units.
The union will vote Thursday and Friday on whether to approve Tosco's contract, but said he could not predict how members would vote.
"It's hard for me to make that call," he said.

Last month, the union said 67 workers would lose jobs at the Wilmington refinery near Los Angeles. About 43 workers would be cut from its Rodeo plant and four from the Santa Maria plant, which feeds some refined product to Rodeo.
Jobs cuts were not slated at the Carson plant, which sends product to the neighboring Wilmington plant for final processing, the union said last month.
